samples.summary: The real `--fresh` delete path is never executed by any test — only the dry-run (which skips it) and the refused-at-the-bound case (which asserts nothing is deleted)
samples.evidence: `cmdReview` deletes round directories at spec-to-pr.mjs:1009-1013 only when `args.fresh && !dryRun` and after the bound lets the run through. Every CLI test that passes `--fresh` either uses `--dry-run` ("review --dry-run --fresh reports the reset round without deleting one", spec-to-pr.test.mjs:434; "review --fresh cannot walk past the bound…", :703 — all runs are `--dry-run`) or is refused at the bound ("review --fresh refused at the bound deletes nothing (real run)", :747, which asserts the rounds SURVIVE). No test performs an under-bound real `review --fresh` and asserts that (a) the pre-existing `round-N` directories are gone, (b) non-round entries in the base survive, and (c) the new round-1 directory does not contain a previous round's lens verdicts. `roundDirsToClear` is unit-tested as a pure name filter (:240) but that assertion holds whether or not `cmdReview` ever calls it, and the wiring test ("review: the round's carry-forward and rebuttals reach the spawned panel", :860) does not pass `--fresh`. If the delete were removed or mis-wired, the suite stays green while `--fresh` silently reuses a stale `round-1` whose old lens `verdict.json` files are then read back by `blockingFindingsIn`/`priorFindingsFor` — stale verdicts reported as this round's.

verdict.reason: The `--fresh` delete at spec-to-pr.mjs:1009-1013 runs only when `args.fresh && !dryRun` AND after the bound check lets the run through (987-997). I searched the whole repo for `--fresh`: only spec-to-pr.test.mjs (plus docs and .agent-review artifacts) uses it. Its three CLI uses are (a) :434 explicit `--dry-run`, (b) :703 whose `run()` helper hard-codes `--dry-run` at :719 for all three invocations including `--fresh --force`, asserting rounds survive at :741, and (c) :747 a real run staged AT the bound, refused before the delete, asserting rounds survive at :775-778. The only unit test, :240, exercises `roundDirsToClear` as a pure name filter and passes regardless of whether cmdReview calls it. The real-run wiring tests that use the recorder panel (:872, :942) never pass `--fresh`. `cmdReview` is not exported (spec-to-pr.mjs:884), `parseArgs` (:351) has no alias or env entry point, and a repo-wide grep for `fresh:`/`fresh =` shows no programmatic invocation — so no in-process path covers it either. The behavior is new in this change: the trusted baseline .trusted/scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs has no `--fresh` anywhere (only an unrelated slug message at :218). Net: a new, destructive-and-state-resetting behavior with zero executing coverage; if the delete were removed or mis-wired, the suite stays green while `--fresh` silently reuses a stale round-1 whose old verdict.json files are read back by blockingFindingsIn (:1112). Major, blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.

Coverage exists only at the two ends (renderBlockingFindings on hand-built entries at spec-to-pr.test.mjs:167-194/618-635; carryForwardFindings on hand-built verdicts at prior-findings.test.mjs:443-562), never through a verdict.json on disk. finding.summary: `cmdReview`'s own wiring — priorFindingsFor → prepareRoundInputs → panelArgs → the spawned panel — is never executed by a test; only the three pieces in isolation are. A break there silently produces a round that reviews without its carry-forward, which is the exact failure the change exists to prevent.
finding.evidence: `prepareRoundInputs` + `panelArgs` are composed in a test (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:560-586), but that composition is done by the TEST, not by `cmdReview`. No test drives `review` past the dry-run return (the panel is spawned via `execFileSync("node", panelArgs(...))` with no injection seam and no stub), so nothing asserts that `cmdReview` passes `inputs.priorFile`/`inputs.rebuttals` rather than, say, the raw `args.rebuttals` path or `null`. The dry-run branch computes `dryPrior` through a separate code path, so even the dry-run tests do not cover the real argv construction. The file's own docblock names this wiring as the gap three rounds kept raising.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims `cmdReview`'s end-to-end wiring (priorFindingsFor → prepareRoundInputs → panelArgs → spawned panel) is never executed by a test, and specifically that there is "no injection seam and no stub". Both parts are false in the working tree.

There IS an injection seam: `panelScript(env)` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:793-796) returns `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` when set, otherwise the sibling `review-panel.mjs`, and `cmdReview` calls `panelScript(process.env)` as the `panel:` argument to `panelArgs` inside the real `execFileSync("node", panelArgs({...}))` (spec-to-pr.mjs:1084-1097).

And there ARE tests that drive `review` past the dry-run return through that seam. scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.test.mjs:811-940 contains a dedicated section ("`cmdReview`'s own wiring, executed rather than re-composed") that builds a throwaway repo with a real `origin/main` (stageBranchAheadOfOrigin, :835-852), stages a round-1 blocking verdict on disk (:879-888), writes a hand-written rebuttals file in check-run-name shape (:891-892), installs a recorder stand-in panel that dumps its argv to disk (writeRecorderPanel, :855-870), then runs the real CLI `node spec-to-pr.mjs review --out base --rebuttals mine.json` with `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` pointed at the recorder (:895-900). It then asserts on the argv the command actually handed the panel: `--prior-findings` equals `<round-2>/prior-findings.json` and that file contains round 1's carried finding (:914-919); `--rebuttals` is the NORMALIZED copy beside the round, explicitly `assert.notEqual(rebuttalArg, rebuttals)` with the lens normalized from `agent-review-security` to `security` (:923-928) — i.e. exactly the "passes inputs.rebuttals rather than raw args.rebuttals" assertion the finding says is missing; plus `--diff-file` content and `--base-sha` against the real merge base (:931-936). A second test (:942-967) asserts round 1 passes NO `--prior-findings` and no `--rebuttals` at all.

The reviewer's searches missed these because the tests reference the seam as `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` (not the string "review-panel"), and the `--prior-findings` assertion at :914 is inside this CLI test, not a panelArgs unit test. This is not a coverage gap.
